subject: Midterm growth split & credit allocation
messages:
From: Emma Barnes <emma@brightline.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Midterm growth question

Hi Irene,

We had a spike this month and expect another predictable surge in Q4. Can you share options for adding incremental capacity mid-contract? Specifically: a) how do we price a 30% top-up for the next 3 months, b) what credit or invoice alignment options there are if we want to annualize later, and c) any SLA implications if we move to a burst bucket.

We need something we can sign quickly — procurement is sensitive to midterm amendments. Happy to hop on a 20-min call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Barnes
Head of Platform, Brightline AI
emma@brightline.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Barnes <emma@brightline.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Midterm growth question

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Emma's note. Brightline is asking for a fast mid-contract top-up (approx +30% usage for 3 months) and wants options for later annualization. Procurement will want clear invoicing and a simple amendment. Can we draft 2 options:

- Option A: Temporary burst bucket (3 months) priced at a blended per-token uplift, no change to co-term, no credits.
- Option B: Top-up as an advance (prepaid) with a carry-forward credit if they annualize within 6 months (applied pro-rata across remaining term).

Key constraints: procurement needs an amendment doc they can sign; finance needs invoice timing spelled out; CS/SRE want SLA impact (if any) — flag if burst affects latency SLO.

Can you take point on numbers and a short SOW? I'll loop legal if we need a small amendment.

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Account Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Barnes <emma@brightline.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Midterm growth question — options attached

Emma — thanks for the quick context. Apologies for the delay — ran the numbers with finance and SRE. Attached a concise options packet and a draft SOW for the amendment (Brightline_Midterm_Options_v1.pdf, SOW-draft.docx). High level: 

Option A — Short burst (recommended if they want zero paperwork):
- 3-month burst bucket sized at +30% of current committed units
- Pricing: +22% per-token uplift on top of existing list rate (applies to tokens consumed from the burst bucket only)
- Invoicing: monthly pay-as-you-go (no prepayment)
- Credits: none
- SLA: no change to core latency SLO; burst requests will be routed to surplus capacity with standard best-effort prioritization

Option B — Prepaid top-up with carry-forward credit (recommended if they want path to annualize):
- Prepay for 3 months of +30% capacity at a blended 18% uplift vs list (upfront invoice)
- If Brightline elects to annualize any portion within 180 days, we convert prepaid units to a committed uplift at a blended true-up price and apply remaining prepaid value as a credit across the new committed term (pro-rata)
- Invoicing: 100% upfront, separate amendment & PO needed
- SLA: same as Option A, but we can include a limited SLA carveout for dedicated burst capacity if they upgrade to a Dedicated pool (requires legal/ops approval)

Recommended path to close quickly: present Option B as primary (prepaid) but give procurement the Option A fallback for speed. I attached suggested amendment language and a short walk-through slide.

Next steps: 
- If this looks good to you, Emma, I'll generate an amendment and an invoice estimate.
- Irene: if we proceed with carveout details (Dedicated burst SLA), can you confirm the ops contacts so SRE can scope?

Attachments: Brightline_Midterm_Options_v1.pdf (2 pages), SOW-draft.docx (1 page stub)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Emma Barnes <emma@brightline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Midterm growth question — options attached

Thanks Ben — this is very helpful. Procurement prefers Option B (prepaid with conversion) as it gives us the best unit economics and a clear path to annualize. A couple of clarifying asks before we sign: 

1) For the conversion math: can you confirm we get a guaranteed floor on the converted committed price (i.e., converted price will not be worse than the blended prepaid rate)?
2) For the invoice: procurement wants the upfront invoice as a single line item they can PO; will Redwood accept a net-30?
3) SLA carveout: we may need a short clause that defines burst priority and a single-point contact for incident ping (does not need full Dedicated commitment). Can you outline that language so legal can review quickly?

If you can get answers on 1–3 by EOD today we can route to procurement and get the PO started. We should be able to sign the amendment this week if the terms are clear.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to do a 15-min call if useful.

Best,
Emma
